newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees 1996 capital expenditures down.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees 1996 capital expenditures down.

text.p: Motorola Inc said on Monday that it expects capital expenditures in 1996 to be about $3.1 billion in 1996, down from $4.2 billion a year ago.
The technology giant also said its businesses are continuing to take actions to reduce operating expenses, while deferring capital expenditures.
The company also said it expects a modest recovery in the semiconductor industry in 1997.

"As was the case in recoveries from previous industry recessions, the improvement in sales and profitability will be gradual at first, as the industry returns to sustainable growth," chief executive officer Gary Tooker said in a news release.

Tooker said the start of the satellite deployment phase of the IRIDIUM program will result in much higher expenses being reported by Iridium LLC, as planned, of which about 25 percent are included in Motorola's financial results.
Iridium is a consortium of companies working to develop a global telecommunications network.

These increased expenses are largely due to satellite depreciation before the system enters commercial service in late 1998, Tooker said, adding that, expenses in the flat panel display business will increase significantly in 1997. These expenses will have an impact on profitability in 1997.
